# Domain Data Models & Schemas

## 📦 Data Structures
The single home of every schema in this repository (**PRINCIPLE-016** R5).

### Task Ledger (`.agents/task_ledger.json`, and `<project>/.aikit/task_ledger.json` per project)
Written only by `scripts/disruption_recovery.py` (locked, atomic; PRINCIPLE-013). `workspace_ledger_path` picks the project's file when the workspace has an `.aikit/` folder (ADR-120); the schema is the same.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | int | Schema version, `1`; `migrate_ledger_schema` fills missing keys. A newer version is refused in place; a missing version is treated as legacy `1` in memory only. |
| `active_task` | object or null | `task_id`, `last_phase` (label), `active_phase` (1-5), `status`, `updated_at` (epoch s), optional `impact_assessment` {`why`, `benefits`, `risks`, `mitigation`}. |
| `checkpoints` | list | At most 20 entries (the active task's plan checkpoint is always kept). Each: `task_id`, `phase`, `phase_num` (1-5), `description`, `files_affected`, `status`, `timestamp`, `timestamp_str`, optional `impact_assessment`. |

`status` values: `in_progress` (recorded by `--checkpoint`), `completed` (`--complete`), `abandoned` (`--reset`), `superseded` (written for the previous task when `--checkpoint` names a different task while it was still `in_progress`; ADR-077). The plan is the latest `phase_num` 2 checkpoint whose `description` starts with `[1/` (PRINCIPLE-004 R1).

### Project Record (`<project>/.aikit/project.json`)
Written once by `write_memory` in `scripts/project_registry.py` when a project is created or first attached; never overwritten afterwards, so a person may edit it. Committed in the project's own repository (ADR-119).

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `schema` | int | `1`; any other value is refused by `load_config`. |
| `name` | string | The project name: 1-64 of `a-z 0-9 - _`, starting with a letter or digit. |
| `test_command` | string or null | Overrides the detected test command; null means detect from the project's files on every call. |
| `gates` | object | Gate name to shell command (adds or replaces a gate) or null (disables a detected one); `secrets` cannot be named. Absent in records written before ADR-122, read as empty. |
| `created` | string | Creation date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. |

The project's decision register is `<project>/.aikit/decisions.md`, created from `DECISIONS_TEMPLATE` with the same entry format as `knowledge/decisions.md`; `latest_decision` ignores the template's commented example.

Stacks and test commands are never stored: `detect_stacks` reads the marker files each time, so they cannot go stale.

### Project Guidelines (`<project>/.aikit/guidelines.md`)
The project tier of PRINCIPLE-001 R4: the project's own rules, written by people or agents, ranked below every principle (PRINCIPLE-000 R6). Created from `GUIDELINES_TEMPLATE`; everything after `## Rules` is one rule per line, `- **G-NNN** (source): rule`, where source is `user`, `ADR-NNN` or a person. IDs are never reused. `guideline_errors` (the guidelines gate) rejects a malformed line, a reused ID, a rule worded to override a principle, and a file over `PROJECT_GUIDELINES_MAX_CHARS`; `add_guideline` refuses the same before writing.

### Attached Projects (`projects/attached.json`)
Local to one AIKit checkout (git-ignored). Lists only folders outside `projects/`; folders inside it are found by their `.aikit/project.json`. Written under `file_lock`, atomically. Unreadable content is an error, never an empty list.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `schema` | int | `1`. |
| `projects` | object | Project name to absolute folder path. |

### Subagent Result Payload
Returned by `delegate_subagent` in `scripts/aikit_cli.py` (`python aikit.py delegate <role> "<task>" --format json`) when executing background tasks delegated to subagents (**PRINCIPLE-008 R1/R6**, **PRINCIPLE-012 R8**).

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | string | `"success"` if process returncode is 0, else `"error"`. |
| `agent` | string | Subagent role invoked (`worker`, `architect`, `coder`, `tester`, `reviewer`, `explorer`). |
| `exit_code` | int | Process exit code (`0` success, `1` operational failure, `2` usage error). |
| `duration_seconds` | float | Execution duration in seconds measured with monotonic clock. |
| `output` | string | Subagent execution findings, suggested diffs, or structured JSON. |
| `ledger_shield` | string | `"unmutated"` confirming task ledgers were shielded against unauthorized modification. |

### Project Report Payload
Printed by `cmd_status` and `cmd_resume` in `scripts/aikit_cli.py` (`python aikit.py status <name> --json`, `python aikit.py resume <name> --json`) so CI and wrappers read a contract instead of parsing the human report (**PRINCIPLE-004 R2/R4**, **PRINCIPLE-011 R5**, ADR-172).

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | bool | `true` when a report was produced; `false` only in the error envelope. |
| `clean` | bool | Delivery readiness, from `project_is_clean`: the same verdict `status --exit-code` returns. `status` only. |
| `project.name` | string | The project as the registry names it. |
| `project.path` | string | Absolute path to the project folder. |
| `project.repo_url` | string or null | Its `origin` remote, or `null` when it is local only. |
| `project.stacks` | list of string | Detected stack names, empty when none was detected. |
| `project.test_command` | string or null | Its test command, or `null` when none is set or detected. |
| `project.latest_decision` | string or null | The newest ADR line in its `.aikit/decisions.md`, or `null`. |
| `project.guidelines` | list of string | Its own rules, verbatim: the rules themselves, never a count, so a JSON cold start cannot lose them. |
| `disruption` | object | The `run_disruption_audit` record for the project, verbatim (see Task Ledger). |
| `ui_task_open` | bool | Whether `.aikit/ui_task.json` exists. `status` only. |
| `gates` | list of string | The Phase 4 gate names `check` would run. `status` only. |
| `error.code` | string | `"project.error"` on an operational or usage failure; `ok` is then `false` and no other key is present. |
| `error.message` | string | The failure's message line; its `Why:`/`Fix:` triad still goes to stderr in text mode. |

## 🛡️ Model Invariants
1. Models are type-annotated; data passed between layers is a frozen dataclass or `NamedTuple` (**PRINCIPLE-009** R5).
2. Every setting has a documented default, so a clone runs with no configuration (**PRINCIPLE-011** R2).

### ADR-173: Credentials Are Refused or Scrubbed at the Write Boundary
- **Date**: 2026-10-22
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: PRINCIPLE-019 R5 makes a leaked credential the one defect with no clean rollback: it must be rotated, never reverted. `check_secrets.py` already treated the task ledger and the dogfood log as scanning surfaces under R3, because this repository's own PRINCIPLE-007 workflow writes `--why`, `--benefits`, `--risks` and `--mitigation` straight into a git-tracked file. But the scanner only reported after the text was already on disk, and in a pre-commit gate that means the value is in the working tree and one `git add` away from permanence. Its pattern table also covered 15 shapes and missed common prefixed formats. Separately, a sub-agent's answer reaches the lead agent's context and anything that logs it, with no scanning surface at all.
- **Decision**:
  1. `SECRET_PATTERNS` gains 13 shapes — GitLab, npm, PyPI, SendGrid, Hugging Face, Google OAuth client secret, Mailgun, Telegram bot, Docker Hub, Notion, Linear, Slack incoming webhook and Azure storage account key — and the private-key block recognizes `ENCRYPTED` and `SSH2 ENCRYPTED` headers. Every addition is anchored on a literal vendor prefix. No bare-length pattern and no PII pattern is added.
  2. `scrub_text(text)` returns the text with each credential-shaped span replaced by `[REDACTED]` plus the detectors that fired. It runs `SECRET_PATTERNS` only, never the entropy fallback or the bare-literal rule, because prose legitimately carries commit hashes and digests. `[REDACTED]` is already in `STRONG_ALLOWLIST`, so scrubbed text is clean when the scanner reads it back.
  3. `checkpoint_command` — the one path both `disruption_recovery.py --checkpoint` and `aikit checkpoint` take (ADR-128) — checks the description and the four impact fields before it reads or writes the ledger. A hit exits 1 and names the detector, the rule and `--redact`. With `--redact` the scrubbed text is recorded instead, and the PRINCIPLE-007 R6 impact validation then runs against the text that will actually be written.
  4. `answer_text` scrubs the sub-agent's answer unconditionally. There is no opt-in, because no caller wants a leaked key verbatim and nothing is lost by redacting one.
  5. `disruption_recovery.py` imports `scrub_text` through both `scripts.check_secrets` and `check_secrets`. It is the only directly-runnable script in the repository with a local import, and every other one is a standalone leaf; the two-form import keeps `python scripts/disruption_recovery.py` working, where only `scripts/` is on `sys.path`, without a `sys.path` bootstrap. If both forms fail the `ImportError` propagates.
- **Consequences**:
  - *Positive*: A credential quoted in an impact note is refused before it reaches a tracked file instead of being found afterwards, which is the only point at which PRINCIPLE-019 R5 can still be satisfied cheaply. Sub-agent output cannot carry a key into the lead agent's context. The pattern table nearly doubles, to 28 shapes, while keeping the near-zero false-positive property the gate's trust depends on; a regression test asserts a risk note citing a commit hash and a `sha256:` digest still scans clean.
  - *Trade-offs*: `--checkpoint` gains a refusal path, so a script that writes credential-shaped free text now exits 1 where it used to succeed. ADR

git commit -q -F - <<'MSG' && git log -1 --format='%H %s'
feat(secrets): refuse or scrub credentials at the write boundary

PRINCIPLE-019 R5 makes a leaked credential the one defect with no clean
rollback. The scanner already treated the ledger as a surface under R3,
because the PRINCIPLE-007 workflow writes --why/--benefits/--risks/
--mitigation straight into a git-tracked file, but it only reported
after the value was already on disk and one `git add` from permanence.

SECRET_PATTERNS grows from 15 to 28 shapes: GitLab, npm, PyPI,
SendGrid, Hugging Face, Google OAuth client secret, Mailgun, Telegram
bot, Docker Hub, Notion, Linear, Slack incoming webhook and Azure
storage account key, plus ENCRYPTED and SSH2 private-key headers. Each
is anchored on a literal vendor prefix; no bare-length or PII pattern
is added, because the gate's trust rests on near-zero false positives.

`scrub_text()` replaces credential-shaped spans with [REDACTED] and
names the detectors. It runs the patterns only, never the entropy
fallback, so a risk note citing a commit hash or a sha256 digest still
scans clean — a regression test pins that.

`checkpoint_command`, the one path both `--checkpoint` and
`aikit checkpoint` take (ADR-128), now checks the description and the
four impact fields before it reads or writes the ledger: a hit exits 1
naming the detector and `--redact`, and `--redact` records the scrubbed
text instead. `answer_text` scrubs sub-agent output unconditionally,
since no caller wants a leaked key verbatim.

disruption_recovery imports scrub_text through both `scripts.` and the
bare module name, so `python scripts/disruption_recovery.py` keeps
working where only scripts/ is on sys.path. It is the first local
import in that module; --help measured 145ms against the 200ms budget.

Pattern detection cannot catch a credential that does not look like
one; ADR-173 records that limit alongside the decisions.

Phase 4 green: 469 tests, rule sync, AST map, reachability, secrets,
test budgets, dogfood 5/5, CLI contract.

content.text: <total_tokens>14940812 tokens left</total_tokens>

Item 2 done — `8604ef0`, verified in isolation, clean tree.

**What shipped**

The scanner went from 15 to 28 credential shapes (GitLab, npm, PyPI, SendGrid, Hugging Face, Google OAuth, Mailgun, Telegram, Docker Hub, Notion, Linear, Slack webhooks, Azure account keys, plus `ENCRYPTED`/`SSH2` private-key headers). All vendor-prefixed — I deliberately added no bare-length or PII patterns, because the file's own design comment is right that a scanner which blocks correct code gets bypassed.

More importantly, detection moved **before** the write. `checkpoint_command` is the single path both `--checkpoint` and `aikit checkpoint` take, so one change covers both: a credential shape in the description or any impact field now exits 1 and names `--redact`, *before* the ledger is read or written. `--redact` records `[REDACTED]` instead. Sub-agent output is scrubbed unconditionally. A regression test pins that a risk note citing a commit hash and a `sha256:` digest still scans clean.

**Three things worth knowing**

**I broke standalone invocation and caught it.** Importing `check_secrets` into `disruption_recovery` worked under `unittest` but broke `python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --help` — every directly-runnable script here is deliberately a standalone leaf, and CI asserts that `--help` exits 0. Fixed with a documented two-form import rather than a `sys.path` bootstrap. `--help` now measures 145 ms against the 200 ms budget; a further import there would need re-measuring.

**A trade-off I'd flag rather than bury.** Patterns that include the key name scrub the name too — `password = "..."` becomes `[REDACTED]`, not `password = "[REDACTED]"`.     """
    The structure PRINCIPLE-005 R1 states, not just its words: a heading, then inside its section
    a `- **Runtime Prerequisites**:` line naming a version and a fenced command right after the
    test-gate label. A substring check passed a README that merely mentioned the labels in prose.
    """
    heading = re.search(r"^(#{1,6}) [^\n]*Cold-Start Quick Reference", readme, re.M)
    if not heading:

    rest = readme[heading.end():]
    following = re.search(rf"^#{{1,{len(heading.group(1))}}} ", rest, re.M)
    section = rest[:following.start()] if following else rest
    errors: List[str] = []
    prerequisites = re.search(r"^- \*\*Runtime Prerequisites\*\*:([^\n]*)", section, re.M)
    if not prerequisites:
        errors.append("the Quick Reference has no line starting '- **Runtime Prerequisites**:' (R1)")

                      "'**Canonical Regression Shield Gate**:' (R1)")

content.content:
1	### 🛠️ Core Operational Command Matrix
     2	| Operational Role | Canonical Command | Verification Gate |
     3	|---|---|---|
     4	| **Manage Projects** | `python aikit.py <cmd>` | `new`, `attach`, `list`, `status`, `check`, `fix` (ADR-119..124) |
     5	| **Run Regression Suite** | `python scripts/check_test_budgets.py` | Both tiers pass; per-test average <=10ms unit, <=350ms integration |
     6	| **Run One Tier** | `python -m unittest tests.test_kit` / `python -m unittest tests.test_integration` | Isolates a failing tier |
     7	| **Synchronize IDE Rules** | `python scripts/sync_principles.py` | <=1,600 est. tokens/target incl. a reserved 300-token Tier 1B |
     8	| **Verify Rule Freshness** | `python scripts/sync_principles.py --check` | Read-only; exits 1 on rule drift, or when a principle changed since the last commit lacks an ADR naming its `--citing` set (PRINCIPLE-000 R3) |
     9	| **Find Principles to Read** | `python scripts/sync_principles.py --involved <paths/commands/output>` | Same answer for every agent (PRINCIPLE-001 R3) |
    10	| **Cross-Principle Check Set** | `python scripts/sync_principles.py --citing <PRINCIPLE-NNN>` | Principles a rule change must be checked against (PRINCIPLE-000 R3) |
    11	| **Update AST & Knowledge** | `python scripts/update_knowledge_base.py` | Rewrites the codebase map, then runs every audit of `--check` below; exits 1 on a syntax error (Python 3.10 grammar) or any audit failure |
    12	| **Verify AST Map Freshness** | `python scripts/update_knowledge_base.py --check` | Read-only; exits 1 on a stale codebase map, README drift (PRINCIPLE-005), an ADR ID out of order, unfinished code (PRINCIPLE-007 R3) or a code-structure violation (PRINCIPLE-009 to PRINCIPLE-011) |
    13	| **Classify Lifecycle Track** | `python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --track` | Prints Track A/B/C of current changes (PRINCIPLE-002 R3) |
    14	| **Audit Disruption Recovery**| `python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --audit` | Clean status check; detects surviving uncommitted files |
    15	| **Resume Interrupted Task** | `python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --resume` | Cold-start command: every `--audit` finding, then the interrupted task, its plan and resumption phase |
    16	| **Record Task Checkpoint**   | `python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --checkpoint <task_id> --phase-num <1-5> --desc <text>` | Appends a checkpoint (PRINCIPLE-002 R4); exits 2 when a task's first plan lacks `--why --benefits --risks --mitigation`, and warns when a task reaches Phase 3 with none (PRINCIPLE-007 R1, R6); exits 1 on credential-shaped text, or records `[REDACTED]` with `--redact` (PRINCIPLE-019 R3) |
    17	| **Complete Task Ledger**     | `python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --complete <task_id>` | Marks the active task completed in `.agents/task_ledger.json`; exits 1, changing nothing, if `<task_id>` is not the active task |
    18	| **Reset Active Task**        | `python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --reset [reason]` | Abandons/clears in-progress task in ledger |
    19	| **Purge Temp Buffers**       | `python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --clean` | Deletes orphaned `*.tmp_*` buffers older than 60 s; younger ones may be a write in progress |
    20	| **Secret Scan Gate** | `python scripts/check_secrets.py --staged\|--commits <range> [--workspace <project>]` | Exits 1 on a credential pattern in the staged diff or agent memory, or when any surface could not be scanned (PRINCIPLE-019) |
    21	| **Verify the Commit Itself** | `python scripts/verify_commit.py` | Runs every gate against the commit alone in a throwaway worktree; exits 1 when the commit holds less than the tree it was tested in (PRINCIPLE-018 R7) |
    22	| **Reachability Shield** | `python scripts/check_reachability.py` | No unwired capability or phantom state key (PRINCIPLE-014 R7) |
    23	| **Operational Dogfood Gate** | `python scripts/dogfood.py` | 5/5 tracks pass; zero host mutation (PRINCIPLE-015) |
    24	| **Discover Any CLI** | `python scripts/<script>.py --help` | Prints usage and exits `0` in <200ms as a fresh process, writing nothing |
    25	| **Sandbox the Ledger CLI** | `python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --workspace <dir> --audit` | Operates on `<dir>/.agents/`, never the repo ledger |
    26	
    27	**Universal CLI contract (PRINCIPLE-011, PRINCIPLE-015).** Every CLI: `--help`/`-h` prints usage, writes nothing, exits `0`; exit `0` success, `1` operational failure, `2` misuse (an unknown flag is refused, never the default); failures print What → Why → Fix on stderr, never a traceback. `--check` is the read-only mode of `sync_principles.py` and `update_knowledge_base.py`.
    28	
    29	---
    30	
    31	## 📦 What's Inside

content.text: The gate parses one path per tree line, so entries can't be merged. But the alignment padding is pure whitespace — let me quantify that first, since it carries no meaning at all.

input.command:
PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python -I - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re
t = Path('README.md').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
block = re.search(r"What's Inside.*?```text\n(.*?)```", t, re.S).group(1)
rows = [l for l in block.split('\n') if '<-' in l]
excess = 0
widest = 0
for l in rows:
    head, _, _ = l.partition('<-')
    stripped = head.rstrip()
    widest = max(widest, len(stripped))
    excess += len(head) - len(stripped)
print(f"tree lines with a comment : {len(rows)}")
print(f"widest entry text         : {widest} chars")
print(f"total alignment spaces    : {excess}")
print(f"if padded to widest+1     : saves {excess - (len(rows)*1) - sum(widest - len(l.partition('<-')[0].rstrip()) for l in rows)} chars")
# what a single-space layout would cost
single = sum(len(l.partition('<-')[0].rstrip()) + 1 + len('<-' + l.partition('<-')[2]) for l in rows)
current = sum(len(l) for l in rows)
print(f"current comment-line bytes: {current}")
print(f"single-space layout bytes : {single}  -> saves {current - single}")
PY

Yes — there was a lot, and it came entirely from whitespace. `749c1b9`.

## What I found

README composition, measured:

| Section | Chars | Editable? |
|---|---|---|
| Principle tables | 5,731 (25.5%) | **No** — generated by `sync_principles.py` from the capsules, which have 0–4 chars of slack |
| "What's Inside" + tree | 4,935 | Tree *membership* is gated; comments are free prose |
| Command matrix | 4,489 | Descriptions are free prose; 5 command strings frozen by the CI-parity test |
| "Start a Project" | 3,864 | Free prose |
| Everything else | 3,466 | Free prose |

A quarter of the file is off limits, and five command strings are frozen verbatim by `test_workflow_commands_match_documented_commands`.

## What I changed — 298 chars, zero words

The tree aligned its `<-` comments at **column 40**, driven by a single 39-character entry while most entries are under 25. That's **930 characters of pure padding**. I plotted the trade-off:

```
column 36:  208 saved,  1 entry overflows
column 34:  309 saved,  3 entries overflow
column 30:  498 saved,  9 entries overflow
column 26:  655 saved, 17 entries overflow
```

Column 36 is the knee — 208 chars for one line losing alignment. Plus a stray blank line inside the tree that broke the `│` spine between `scripts/` and `tests/`, two runs of double blank lines, and padding in hand-written table cells.

**Verified rather than asserted:** comparing the word sequence against HEAD with the table pipe treated as a separator — **2,826 words, identical and in the same order.** Headroom: **15 → 313**.

Two things worth knowing:

**The unit tier caught me overreaching.** My first pass stripped padding from *all* table cells, including the generated principle table, so `sync_readme_table` no longer reproduced the file and two tests failed. Regenerating restored the generator's own spacing — which cost 75 of the 373 chars I'd initially recovered. That's the right outcome: the generated region isn't mine to reformat.

**Entries can't be merged, only shortened.** `audit_readme` parses one path per tree line and requires every tracked entry to appear, so combining `CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md` onto one line would fail the gate. Worth knowing before anyone tries it.

## Still available, if you want it later

Roughly **120 more characters** from genuine redundancy, which I did *not* touch because it changes wording and you asked for no meaning loss:

- Synonym triples in the `knowledge/` tree comments — "Data structures, schemas, and persistence models", "Presentation layer, UI state, and event loops", "Knowledge base table of contents & architecture map" (~90 chars)
- `Read-only;` on two matrix rows, already stated by the Universal CLI contract paragraph below the table (~22 chars)
- `LICENSE <- GNU AGPL-3.0 License` — "License" twice (~8 chars)

The `ui` paragraph is ~1,900 characters in one sentence chain and is the only place with real structural slack, but condensing it is a rewrite with actual meaning risk. I'd leave it unless the budget forces the issue.

**313 characters is enough for items 3 and 4** without touching prose, so I'd stop here. One useful property: if a future edit re-aligns the tree to column 40, `update_knowledge_base.py --check` fails on size — the regression is self-detecting rather than silent.

`verify_commit.py` is running in the background on `749c1b9`; four commits are now unpushed. I'll report the verification and then start item 3 unless you'd rather reorder.

def format_resume_report(audit: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """
    The one cold-start report (PRINCIPLE-004 R2): every --audit finding, then where to resume.
    It used to print only the interrupted task, so with no active task it said "Ready for a new
    task" over uncommitted, untracked or quarantined files that --audit would have shown.
    """
    lines = [
        "============================================================",
        "⚡ DISRUPTION RESUMPTION GUIDANCE (PRINCIPLE-006)",
        "============================================================",
    ]
    lines += audit_body_lines(audit)
    if audit.get("conflicted_files"):
        lines.append("⛔ BLOCKED: resolve the conflicts above before any other action.")

    if audit.get("ledger_error"):
        lines.append("⛔ BLOCKED: this ledger cannot be read by this AIKit; no task state was changed.")
        lines.append("============================================================")
        return "\n".join(lines)

    interrupted = audit.get("interrupted_task")
    if not interrupted:
        if audit.get("modified_files") or audit.get("untracked_files") or audit.get("dangling_temp_files"):
            lines.append("🟡 No interrupted task, but the files above are uncommitted: inspect them before a new task and never overwrite them.")
        elif not audit.get("conflicted_files"):
            lines.append("🟢 No interrupted task detected. Ready for a new task.")
        lines.append("============================================================")
        return "\n".join(lines)

    task_id = interrupted.get("task_id", "unknown")
    phase = interrupted.get("last_phase", "unknown")
    phase_num = resolve_active_phase(interrupted, default=2)
    # PRINCIPLE-002 R4 records a checkpoint on ENTERING a phase, so the recorded phase is the one
    # in progress: resume there. Guessing "phase + 1" when the tree was clean skipped work - after
    # a PRINCIPLE-006 milestone commit during Phase 3, it sent the agent straight to Phase 4.
    next_phase_num = phase_num
    
    lines.append(f"⚠️  RESUMING INTERRUPTED TASK: '{task_id}'")
    lines.append(f"📌 Last Active Phase: Phase {phase_num} ({phase})")
    lines.append(f"🚀 Recommended Resumption Phase: Phase {next_phase_num}")
    if audit.get("plan"):
        lines.append(f"🗺️  Plan (Phase 2 checkpoint): {audit['plan']}")
    if audit.get("dangling_temp_files"):
        lines.append(f"🧹 Action Needed: Purge {len(audit['dangling_temp_files'])} dangling .tmp_* files (run 'python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --clean')")
    lines.append(f"💡 Next Action: Inspect surviving files, run unit tests, and resume at Phase {next_phase_num}")
    lines.append("============================================================")
    return "\n".join(lines)


VALID_COMMIT_TYPES = {
    "feat",
    "fix",
    "refactor",
    "docs",
    "chore",
    "test",
    "perf",
    "build",
    "ci",
}

def impact_errors(description: str, phase_num: Optional[int], fields: Dict[str, Optional[str]],
                  has_prior_impact: bool) -> List[str]:
    """
    PRINCIPLE-007 R6: a task's first plan checkpoint (Phase 2, `--desc` starting `[1/`) carries the
    whole impact assessment, and `--risks` gives a verdict for each blast-radius dimension of R2.
    Plans used to be recorded with `--why` alone, or nothing, and nothing noticed.
    """
    if phase_num != 2 or not description.startswith("[1/") or has_prior_impact:
        return []
    errors = [f"--{name} is required on the first plan checkpoint" for name, value in fields.items()
              if not (value or "").strip()]
    risks = (fields.get("risks") or "").lower()
    if risks.strip():
        errors += [f"--risks must give a verdict for '{label}' (write 'none' when there is no risk)"
                   for label in RISK_DIMENSIONS if label not in risks]
    return errors

    """

    write one can write the other. A value may contain `:` - only the first one in a segment
    separates the key - and empty segments are ignored, so a trailing `;` is not an error.
    """
    if len(text) > MAX_HANDOFF_CHARS:

    return packet, errors

                          handoff: str = "") -> Tuple[str, Dict[str, Optional[str]], str, List[str]]:
    """
    The checkpoint's free text, scrubbed when `redact` is set, plus the detectors that fired.

    PRINCIPLE-019 R3 makes the ledger a secret-scanning surface because `--why`, `--benefits`,
    `--risks` and `--mitigation` are written into a git-tracked file; R5 makes such a leak
    unrecoverable. Checking here, in the one path both CLIs take (ADR-128), refuses the write
    instead of reporting it afterwards (ADR-173).
    """
    detectors: List[str] = []
    scrubbed_desc, hits = scrub_text(desc or "")
    detectors.extend(hits)
    scrubbed_impact: Dict[str, Optional[str]] = {}
    for field, value in impact.items():
        if not value:
            scrubbed_impact[field] = value
            continue
        scrubbed_value, hits = scrub_text(value)
        detectors.extend(f"{name} in --{field}" for name in hits)
        scrubbed_impact[field] = scrubbed_value
    if not redact:
        return desc, impact, detectors
    return scrubbed_desc, scrubbed_impact, detectors

# Domain Data Models & Schemas

## 📦 Data Structures
The single home of every schema in this repository (**PRINCIPLE-016** R5).

### Task Ledger (`.agents/task_ledger.json`, and `<project>/.aikit/task_ledger.json` per project)
Written only by `scripts/disruption_recovery.py` (locked, atomic; PRINCIPLE-013). `workspace_ledger_path` picks the project's file when the workspace has an `.aikit/` folder (ADR-120); the schema is the same.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | int | Schema version, `1`; `migrate_ledger_schema` fills missing keys. A newer version is refused in place; a missing version is treated as legacy `1` in memory only. |
| `active_task` | object or null | `task_id`, `last_phase` (label), `active_phase` (1-5), `status`, `updated_at` (epoch s), optional `impact_assessment` {`why`, `benefits`, `risks`, `mitigation`}. |
| `checkpoints` | list | At most 20 entries (the active task's plan checkpoint is always kept). Each: `task_id`, `phase`, `phase_num` (1-5), `description`, `files_affected`, `status`, `timestamp`, `timestamp_str`, optional `impact_assessment`. |

`description` and the four `impact_assessment` fields are free text written into a git-tracked file, so a credential shape in any of them makes `--checkpoint` exit 1 before the ledger is read or written; `--redact` records the span as `[REDACTED]` instead (PRINCIPLE-019 R3, ADR-173).

`status` values: `in_progress` (recorded by `--checkpoint`), `completed` (`--complete`), `abandoned` (`--reset`), `superseded` (written for the previous task when `--checkpoint` names a different task while it was still `in_progress`; ADR-077). The plan is the latest `phase_num` 2 checkpoint whose `description` starts with `[1/` (PRINCIPLE-004 R1).

### Project Record (`<project>/.aikit/project.json`)
Written once by `write_memory` in `scripts/project_registry.py` when a project is created or first attached; never overwritten afterwards, so a person may edit it. Committed in the project's own repository (ADR-119).

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `schema` | int | `1`; any other value is refused by `load_config`. |
| `name` | string | The project name: 1-64 of `a-z 0-9 - _`, starting with a letter or digit. |
| `test_command` | string or null | Overrides the detected test command; null means detect from the project's files on every call. |
| `gates` | object | Gate name to shell command (adds or replaces a gate) or null (disables a detected one); `secrets` cannot be named. Absent in records written before ADR-122, read as empty. |
| `created` | string | Creation date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. |

The project's decision register is `<project>/.aikit/decisions.md`, created from `DECISIONS_TEMPLATE` with the same entry format as `knowledge/decisions.md`; `latest_decision` ignores the template's commented example.

Stacks and test commands are never stored: `detect_stacks` reads the marker files each time, so they cannot go stale.

### Project Guidelines (`<project>/.aikit/guidelines.md`)
The project tier of PRINCIPLE-001 R4: the project's own rules, written by people or agents, ranked below every principle (PRINCIPLE-000 R6). Created from `GUIDELINES_TEMPLATE`; everything after `## Rules` is one rule per line, `- **G-NNN** (source): rule`, where source is `user`, `ADR-NNN` or a person. IDs are never reused. `guideline_errors` (the guidelines gate) rejects a malformed line, a reused ID, a rule worded to override a principle, and a file over `PROJECT_GUIDELINES_MAX_CHARS`; `add_guideline` refuses the same before writing.

### Attached Projects (`projects/attached.json`)
Local to one AIKit checkout (git-ignored). Lists only folders outside `projects/`; folders inside it are found by their `.aikit/project.json`. Written under `file_lock`, atomically. Unreadable content is an error, never an empty list.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `schema` | int | `1`. |
| `projects` | object | Project name to absolute folder path. |

### Subagent Result Payload
Returned by `delegate_subagent` in `scripts/aikit_cli.py` (`python aikit.py delegate <role> "<task>" --format json`) when executing background tasks delegated to subagents (**PRINCIPLE-008 R1/R6**, **PRINCIPLE-012 R8**).

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | string | `"success"` if process returncode is 0, else `"error"`. |
| `agent` | string | Subagent role invoked (`worker`, `architect`, `coder`, `tester`, `reviewer`, `explorer`). |
| `exit_code` | int | Process exit code (`0` success, `1` operational failure, `2` usage error). |
| `duration_seconds` | float | Execution duration in seconds measured with monotonic clock. |
| `output` | string | Subagent execution findings, suggested diffs, or structured JSON. |
| `ledger_shield` | string | `"unmutated"` confirming task ledgers were shielded against unauthorized modification. |

### Project Report Payload
Printed by `cmd_status` and `cmd_resume` in `scripts/aikit_cli.py` (`python aikit.py status <name> --json`, `python aikit.py resume <name> --json`) so CI and wrappers read a contract instead of parsing the human report (**PRINCIPLE-004 R2/R4**, **PRINCIPLE-011 R5**, ADR-172).

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | bool | `true` when a report was produced; `false` only in the error envelope. |
| `clean` | bool | Delivery readiness, from `project_is_clean`: the same verdict `status --exit-code` returns. `status` only. |
| `project.name` | string | The project as the registry names it. |
| `project.path` | string | Absolute path to the project folder. |
| `project.repo_url` | string or null | Its `origin` remote, or `null` when it is local only. |
| `project.stacks` | list of string | Detected stack names, empty when none was detected. |
| `project.test_command` | string or null | Its test command, or `null` when none is set or detected. |
| `project.latest_decision` | string or null | The newest ADR line in its `.aikit/decisions.md`, or `null`. |
| `project.guidelines` | list of string | Its own rules, verbatim: the rules themselves, never a count, so a JSON cold start cannot lose them. |
| `disruption` | object | The `run_disruption_audit` record for the project, verbatim (see Task Ledger). |
| `ui_task_open` | bool | Whether `.aikit/ui_task.json` exists. `status` only. |
| `gates` | list of string | The Phase 4 gate names `check` would run. `status` only. |
| `error.code` | string | `"project.error"` on an operational or usage failure; `ok` is then `false` and no other key is present. |
| `error.message` | string | The failure's message line; its `Why:`/`Fix:` triad still goes to stderr in text mode. |

## 🛡️ Model Invariants
1. Models are type-annotated; data passed between layers is a frozen dataclass or `NamedTuple` (**PRINCIPLE-009** R5).
2. Every setting has a documented default, so a clone runs with no configuration (**PRINCIPLE-011** R2).
3. A persisted model carries a version key (`version` in the ledger) and a migration function that fills missing keys (**PRINCIPLE-013** R4). A reader refuses an unsupported newer version without modifying or quarantining the file; a missing version is accepted only through a documented legacy migration.

### ADR-174: The Checkpoint Carries a Cold-Start Handoff Packet
- **Date**: 2026-10-22
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: `--resume` prints the plan (PRINCIPLE-004 R1) but nothing about progress against it. Resuming `aikit-scaffold-lint-fixes-v1` this session meant reading a git diff to learn which of its six milestones were already done, because the ledger had no place to say so. Three other things had no home either: an approach already tried and rejected, which a resumed agent is free to repeat; a question put to the user and still unanswered, which a compaction simply erases; and what had already been verified, so Phase 4 is either redone blindly or trusted blindly. `format_resume_report`'s own "Next Action" line was a hardcoded string telling every task to inspect surviving files and run the unit tier, which is the same generic-default defect class `check_reachability.py` was built after.
- **Decision**:
  1. A checkpoint may carry an optional `handoff` object with the keys `next` (required), `state`, `failed`, `open` and `evidence`.
  2. `--handoff` takes one string of `key: value` segments separated by `;`, the format `--risks` already uses, so an agent that can write one can write the other. Only the first `:` in a segment separates the key, so a value may contain colons; empty segments are ignored; an unknown key or a missing `next` exits 2 and names the accepted keys; the input is bounded to 2,000 characters.
  3. **No ledger schema version bump.** `validate_ledger_version` refuses any version that is not exactly `LEDGER_SCHEMA_VERSION`, including an older one, so bumping to 2 would have made AIKit's own ledger and all 20 registered projects' ledgers unreadable. The change is purely additive instead: the key is absent unless given, every reader uses `.get()`, and an older build ignores it harmlessly.
  4. The packet's text passes through the ADR-173 credential gate with the description and the impact fields, so `--handoff` is not a new way to write a credential into a tracked file.
  5. `--resume` prints the latest packet belonging to the active task — an older one describes a state already moved past — and uses its `next` in place of the generic Next Action line. A task with no packet keeps the old line, so nothing is lost for a task that records none.
- **Consequences**:
  - *Positive*: A resumed agent reads what was done, what failed, what is open and what to do next instead of re-deriving it from a diff. An unanswered user question survives compaction. The cold-start Next Action becomes task-specific. One flag and one parser, consistent with an existing validated format.
  - *Trade-offs*: `aikit checkpoint` and `--checkpoint` gain a flag, and `--resume` gains up to four lines of output against PRINCIPLE-004 R5's 100-line budget; a test pins the report inside it. The packet is the agent's own account of its work: unlike a test or a hash, nothing can verify that `failed` or `evidence` is true, so it is a memory aid and never evidence in the PRINCIPLE-014 sense. `next` is required, which makes a packet that only answers "what failed" impossible to record — deliberate, since a packet with no next action does not help a cold start.
  - *Limitation*: Only 20 checkpoints are retained, so a packet older than that window is pruned with its checkpoint. The plan checkpoint is exempt from pruning; a handoff is not.
- **Reported, not fixed here**: `validate_ledger_version` refusing *older* versions contradicts `knowledge/data_models.md`, which states that only a newer version is refused in place. The two have been indistinguishable because the version has only ever been 1. Any future bump that genuinely needs one must fix that first, or every existing ledger becomes unreadable. Left out of this task under PRINCIPLE-007 R4.
- Cross-principle check: no principle section changed. The mechanisms serve PRINCIPLE-004 R1, R2 and R5 (the cold-start report, bounded), PRINCIPLE-005 R2 (README documents the flag in the same commit), PRINCIPLE-006 (resumption after disruption), PRINCIPLE-011 R5 (exit 2 for a malformed packet), PRINCIPLE-013 R4 (no schema break; the existing migration is untouched), PRINCIPLE-014 R1 (a failing-first test per behaviour) and PRINCIPLE-016 R5 (the fields are written only to `knowledge/data_models.md`).
ADR

+### ADR-174: The Checkpoint Carries a Cold-Start Handoff Packet

+- **Context**: `--resume` prints the plan (PRINCIPLE-004 R1) but nothing about progress against it. Resuming `aikit-scaffold-lint-fixes-v1` this session meant reading a git diff to learn which of its six milestones were already done, because the ledger had no place to say so. Three other things had no home either: an approach already tried and rejected, which a resumed agent is free to repeat; a question put to the user and still unanswered, which a compaction simply erases; and what had already been verified, so Phase 4 is either redone blindly or trusted blindly. `format_resume_report`'s own "Next Action" line was a hardcoded string telling every task to inspect surviving files and run the unit tier, which is the same generic-default defect class `check_reachability.py` was built after.
+  1. A checkpoint may carry an optional `handoff` object with the keys `next` (required), `state`, `failed`, `open` and `evidence`.

+  2. `--handoff` takes one string of `key: value` segments separated by `;`, the format `--risks` already uses, so an agent that can write one can write the other. Only the first `:` in a segment separates the key, so a value may contain colons; empty segments are ignored; an unknown key or a missing `next` exits 2 and names the accepted keys; the input is bounded to 2,000 characters.

+  3. **No ledger schema version bump.** `validate_ledger_version` refuses any version that is not exactly `LEDGER_SCHEMA_VERSION`, including an older one, so bumping to 2 would have made AIKit's own ledger and all 20 registered projects' ledgers unreadable. The change is purely additive instead: the key is absent unless given, every reader uses `.get()`, and an older build ignores it harmlessly.
+  4. The packet's text passes through the ADR-173 credential gate with the description and the impact fields, so `--handoff` is not a new way to write a credential into a tracked file.

+  5. `--resume` prints the latest packet belonging to the active task — an older one describes a state already moved past — and uses its `next` in place of the generic Next Action line. A task with no packet keeps the old line, so nothing is lost for a task that records none.

+  - *Positive*: A resumed agent reads what was done, what failed, what is open and what to do next instead of re-deriving it from a diff. An unanswered user question survives compaction. The cold-start Next Action becomes task-specific. One flag and one parser, consistent with an existing validated format.

+  - *Trade-offs*: `aikit checkpoint` and `--checkpoint` gain a flag, and `--resume` gains up to four lines of output against PRINCIPLE-004 R5's 100-line budget; a test pins the report inside it. The packet is the agent's own account of its work: unlike a test or a hash, nothing can verify that `failed` or `evidence` is true, so it is a memory aid and never evidence in the PRINCIPLE-014 sense. `next` is required, which makes a packet that only answers "what failed" impossible to record — deliberate, since a packet with no next action does not help a cold start.
+  - *Limitation*: Only 20 checkpoints are retained, so a packet older than that window is pruned with its checkpoint. The plan checkpoint is exempt from pruning; a handoff is not.

+- **Reported, not fixed here**: `validate_ledger_version` refusing *older* versions contradicts `knowledge/data_models.md`, which states that only a newer version is refused in place. The two have been indistinguishable because the version has only ever been 1. Any future bump that genuinely needs one must fix that first, or every existing ledger becomes unreadable. Left out of this task under PRINCIPLE-007 R4.

+- Cross-principle check: no principle section changed. feat(ledger): carry a cold-start handoff packet on checkpoints

`--resume` printed the plan but nothing about progress against it.
Resuming aikit-scaffold-lint-fixes-v1 this session meant reading a git
diff to learn which of its six milestones were done, because the ledger
had nowhere to say so. Three other things had no home either: an
approach already tried and rejected, which a resumed agent is free to
repeat; a question put to the user and still unanswered, which a
compaction erases; and what had already been verified. The "Next
Action" line was a hardcoded string telling every task to inspect
surviving files and run the unit tier.

A checkpoint may now carry an optional `handoff` object with `next`
(required), `state`, `failed`, `open` and `evidence`. `--handoff` takes
one string of `key: value` segments separated by `;` — the format
`--risks` already uses — on both `--checkpoint` and `aikit checkpoint`,
through the one checkpoint_command path. A value may contain colons; an
unknown key or a missing `next` exits 2 naming the accepted keys; input
is bounded to 2,000 chars. `--resume` prints the active task's latest
packet and uses its `next` in place of the generic line.

No ledger schema version bump, deliberately: validate_ledger_version
refuses any version that is not exactly current, including an older
one, so bumping to 2 would have made AIKit's own ledger and all 20
registered projects' ledgers unreadable. The change is additive — the
key is absent unless given, every reader uses .get(), and an older
build ignores it.

The packet passes through the ADR-173 credential gate with the
description and impact fields, so it is not a new way to write a
credential into a tracked file.

check_reachability.py rejected the first implementation: the keys were
written by a comprehension over HANDOFF_KEYS, which hides every literal
producer. They are now written key by key, which is what makes the
shield's guarantee real and documents the schema where it is written.

ADR-174 records the decisions, the limits, and two gate defects found
while doing this and deliberately left unfixed under PRINCIPLE-007 R4.

Phase 4 green: 478 tests, rule sync, AST map, reachability, secrets,
test budgets, dogfood 5/5, CLI contract.

Item 4 done — `278f3f5`, verified in isolation, clean tree.

I picked item 4 over item 3 deliberately: you said continue, not that I should edit the governance surface, and item 3 rewrites generated rule text in all eight Tier-1 files. That still needs your explicit go-ahead.

**What shipped.** A checkpoint can now carry a `handoff` object — `next` (required), `state`, `failed`, `open`, `evidence` — via one `--handoff "key: value; key: value"` flag on both CLI surfaces, in the same format `--risks` already uses. `--resume` prints the active task's latest packet and uses its `next` in place of the generic line. It's dogfooded: I recorded this task's own handoff and read it back out of `--resume`.

**I was wrong about the schema bump, and it would have been bad.** My proposal said "schema v2 + migration". Reading `validate_ledger_version` first: it refuses **any** version that isn't exactly current, *including older ones*. Bumping to 2 would have made AIKit's own ledger and all 20 registered projects' ledgers unreadable — `--resume`, `--audit`, `aikit status` and `aikit check` would all have failed. The handoff is purely additive, so it needs no bump: the key is absent unless given, every reader uses `.get()`, and an older build ignores it.

**The reachability shield rejected my first implementation, correctly.** I wrote the keys with a comprehension over `HANDOFF_KEYS`, which hides every literal producer, so `handoff['next']` read as a phantom key. Writing them key by key is what makes the shield's guarantee real.

**Two defects found in the gates themselves, reported not fixed** (P-007 R4 — outside this task's plan; both are in ADR-174):

1. `validate_ledger_version` refusing *older* versions contradicts `knowledge/data_models.md`, which says only a newer version is refused in place. They've been indistinguishable because the version has only ever been 1. **Any future bump that genuinely needs one must fix this first**, or every existing ledger breaks.
2. `check_reachability.py:264` — `all_literals` is a `set`, so `sum(1 for lit in all_literals if lit == key)` can never exceed 1. The "a key appearing more than once has a producer" fallback is dead code, and its comment claims behaviour it doesn't have. Direction is safe (false positives, not false negatives), but it makes the gate stricter than documented.

One honest limit on the feature itself: unlike a test or a hash, nothing can verify that `failed` or `evidence` is true. It's a memory aid, never evidence in the P-014 sense, and ADR-174 says so.

**Five commits, all verified in isolation, none pushed:** `e6e708b`, `e18a1b3`, `8604ef0`, `749c1b9`, `278f3f5`. README headroom is **196 characters**.

Next up is **item 3, the Tier-1 pointer** — one line in each of the eight targets so they reference `SKILL.md`, fixing the gap where the only budget-free home for rules is invisible to 6 of 8 hosts. It edits generated governance text and consumes part of the 0–4 character capsule slack, so I'd like your explicit yes before starting. Want me to proceed with it, fix either gate defect instead, or push what's here?

def render_tier1_target(heading: str, principles: List[Dict], domain_rules: str = "") -> str:
    """
    Render one always-injected Tier 1 target (PRINCIPLE-001 R1/R3, PRINCIPLE-017 R2).

    The header deliberately says *when* to read Tier 2, not merely *that* it exists. The former
    "Strictly follow all principles defined in AGENTS.md and GUIDELINES.md" invited agents to
    load ~27k tokens of Tier 2 up front - the exact bloat PRINCIPLE-001 exists to prevent. It also
    marks the file as generated, so a hand edit is not silently overwritten by the next sync.
    """
    lines = [
        heading,
        "",
        # Wording mirrors PRINCIPLE-001 R1 (precedence) and R3 (trigger names) exactly; a test
        # keeps the two in lock-step so every agent receives the same instruction.
        f"> Generated from `{SSOT_MD.name}` by `scripts/sync_principles.py`; do not edit.",
        "> Capsules bind; `GUIDELINES.md` wins on conflict. On a contract change, failure or "
        "ambiguity, read the `### PRINCIPLE-NNN:` section of each principle "
        "`sync_principles.py --involved` lists; never the whole file unless asked.",
        "",
        "## Core Principles",
    ]
    for p in principles:
        label = f"{p['id']} {tier1_title(p['title'])}"
        summary = p.get("invariant") or p.get("concept")
        # Plain labels: bold markers are decoration (PRINCIPLE-001 R7), ~4 chars x every line.
        lines.append(f"- {label}: {summary}")
    lines.append("")
    append_domain_rules(lines, domain_rules)
    return "\n".join(lines)

cat >> knowledge/decisions.md <<'ADR'


### ADR-175: The Tier 1 Header Stops Naming Its Own Generator
- **Date**: 2026-10-22
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: The Tier 1 context budget is 1,600 estimated tokens per target, and PRINCIPLE-001's headroom rule requires the universal rules to still fit with a full 1,200-character Tier 1B block, so the real limit is 6,403 characters of rendered text. Measured across all eight targets, the worst (`.agents/rules/principles.md`) sat at 6,400: **three characters free**. That blocks any further Tier 1 text, including the `.agents/skills/aikit/SKILL.md` pointer the kit needs because the operational runbook is auto-discovered by only two of the eight supported hosts and no Tier 1 file references it. The header's first line spent 32 of those characters on ``by `scripts/sync_principles.py` ``, which the same rendered file already states twice: the PRINCIPLE-017 capsule names `scripts/sync_principles.py`, and the next header line names `sync_principles.py --involved`.
- **Decision**:
  1. The Tier 1 header reads ``> Generated from `GUIDELINES.md`; do not edit.`` The generator's name is not repeated.
  2. A test pins the three facts that make the removal lossless: the rendered target still matches `is_generated_target`, it still contains `scripts/sync_principles.py` through the PRINCIPLE-017 capsule, and it still contains `sync_principles.py --involved`. If any of them stops holding, the header has to name the generator again.
  3. No principle section changed, so no cross-principle check set applies. The text lives in `render_tier1_target`, not in `GUIDELINES.md`.
- **Consequences**:
  - *Positive*: The worst target drops from 6,400 to 6,368 characters and the budget margin goes from 3 to 35, without removing any information from the file. Eight host instruction surfaces get one line shorter.
  - *Trade-offs*: The `Generated from ` prefix is a `GENERATED_MARKERS` entry, so the phrase is load-bearing for PRINCIPLE-017 R2's refusal to overwrite a file it did not generate; the test asserts it rather than trusting the wording. A reader who wants the regeneration command now finds it one line down or in the PRINCIPLE-017 capsule instead of on the first line.
- **Does not resolve the pointer**: 35 characters is still not enough to add the runbook pointer safely. Measured candidates: ``Runbook: `.agents/skills/aikit/SKILL.md`.`` overruns by 7; the bare path overruns by 4; `See .agents/skills/aikit/SKILL.md` fits with 1 character to spare and `Runbook: .agents/skills/aikit/` with 4. A one-character margin on the gate that blocks every commit is a tripwire, not a design, and the phrasings that fit are the vaguest. Adding the pointer therefore needs a deliberate budget decision — raising `TARGET_TOKEN_BUDGET`, lowering `MAX_DOMAIN_CHARS` at the adopter's expense, or condensing capsule text — and is left to one.
- Cross-principle check: no principle section changed. The change serves PRINCIPLE-001 R1 (the per-target budget it exists to protect), PRINCIPLE-005 R2 (no documented command, flag or exit code changed, so README is untouched), PRINCIPLE-014 R1 (the output change carries a failing-first test) and PRINCIPLE-017 R2 (all eight targets regenerated; the generated-file marker preserved).
ADR

**What I did ship.** The Tier-1 header was spending 32 of the budget's last characters naming its own generator, which the same rendered file already states twice (the P-017 capsule names `scripts/sync_principles.py`; the next line names `sync_principles.py --involved`). Removing it took the worst target from 6,400 to 6,368 of 6,403 — **margin 3 → 35 characters, with no information lost from the file.** A test pins the three facts that make it lossless, including that `is_generated_target` still matches, since losing the `Generated from ` prefix would stop sync recognising its own output.

**What I did not ship, and why.** Item 3 doesn't fit. I measured all five phrasings against the worst of the eight targets:

| Pointer | Margin |
|---|---|
| ``Runbook: `.agents/skills/aikit/SKILL.md`.`` | **−7** |
| `Commands: .agents/skills/aikit/SKILL.md` | **−5** |
| `Runbook: .agents/skills/aikit/SKILL.md` | **−4** |
| `See .agents/skills/aikit/SKILL.md` | **+1** |
| `Runbook: .agents/skills/aikit/` | **+4** |

Only the two vaguest fit, at one and four characters. `sync_principles.py --check` gates every commit in this repo, so a one-character margin means the next capsule word breaks the build for all work, not just rule work. I'm not shipping that, and the phrasings that do fit are the ones least likely to actually send an agent to the file.

**So the pointer needs a budget decision, which is yours:**

- **Raise `TARGET_TOKEN_BUDGET` 1600 → 1650.** Honest fix: the number was set when there were fewer principles, and 19 capsules now consume nearly all of it. Track C, numeric limit in `GUIDELINES.md`, so an ADR plus P-001's full cross-principle check. Costs ~50 tokens in every host's context, every session.
- **Lower `MAX_DOMAIN_CHARS` 1200 → 1100.** Cheapest mechanically, but it takes 100 characters from the *adopter's* allowance — precisely the harm the headroom rule exists to prevent, and `sync_principles.py:378` names that failure mode in a comment.
- **Condense capsule text to free ~45 characters.** Third time this session the answer is "cut prose". Touches principle sections, so it needs the cross-principle check, and it's the option that degrades the rules themselves.
- **Drop the pointer.** Accept that the runbook reaches 2 of 8 hosts and that `SKILL.md` is not a usable home for rules. That makes items like the reuse ladder unaffordable permanently.

class UnsupportedLedgerVersion(Exception):
    """
    A ledger declares a schema this build cannot read (PRINCIPLE-013 R4, PRINCIPLE-016 R5).

    Deliberately neither OSError nor ValueError: load_ledger() treats those as corruption and
    would quarantine or replace the file. A newer format is valid data, so it is refused in place.
    """

    def __init__(self, path: Path, found: Any, supported: int) -> None:
        self.path = Path(path)
        self.found = found
        self.supported = supported
        self.why = ("the ledger was written by a different AIKit whose format this build does not "
                    "understand; reading or rewriting it could lose task history")
        self.fix = ("open it with the AIKit version that wrote it, or restore a ledger written in "
                    "schema version " + str(supported) + "; the file was not modified")
        super().__init__(
            f"{self.path} declares ledger schema version {found!r}; this AIKit reads version {supported}\n"
            f"Why: {self.why}\nFix: {self.fix}"
        )

def locked_ledger(
    ledger_file: Optional[Path] = None,
    timeout_seconds: float = LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
    poll_interval: float = 0.05,
):
    """
    Serialize a full read-modify-write cycle on the task ledger (PRINCIPLE-013 Rule 3).

    Yields the loaded ledger; the caller mutates it in place and the ledger is saved on clean
    exit, all while holding the advisory lock. Without this, parallel subagents interleave
    load/save cycles and silently erase each other's checkpoints (lost-update race).

    Contention is surfaced, never swallowed: if the lock cannot be acquired within the bounded
    timeout the mutation is abandoned with a diagnostic rather than written unprotected.
    """
    path = Path(ledger_file) if ledger_file is not None else LEDGER_PATH
    with file_lock(path, timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds, poll_interval=poll_interval) as acquired:
        if not acquired:
            raise TimeoutError(
                f"[PRINCIPLE-013 LOCK CONTENTION] Could not acquire advisory lock on "
                f"{path.name} within {timeout_seconds}s. "
                f"Why: another agent or process is mid-write on the ledger. "
                f"Fix: retry shortly, or remove a stale '{path.name}.lock' if no process is active."
            )

An explicit user instruction overrides exactly two things in this principle: the R3 obligation to read a section, and the R3 ban on loading `GUIDELINES.md` in full. It does not override another principle: a conflict between a user instruction and another principle is decided by that principle's own rules, including PRINCIPLE-002 R5.

It MUST name every command, script, file path, numeric threshold and named gate that the principle's *[Agent]* rules require an agent to run or respect. It MUST NOT contain rationale, examples, or adjectives that name no mechanism. Deletion test: a phrase whose removal loses no command, path, number or named rule MUST be removed.
  3. **Tier 2 Retrieval Triggers** *[Agent]*: When a trigger below occurs, the agent MUST read the `GUIDELINES.md` section of every involved principle before any further file edit or commit, and before running any command other than those needed to compute the involved principles and read their sections. A principle is *involved* when a backtick-quoted name in its capsule (a file, path, script or command) occurs verbatim in the paths the agent will change, the commands it will run, or the failing output, or when that text contains the principle's ID; when nothing matches, the involved principle is PRINCIPLE-003. `python scripts/sync_principles.py --involved <text>` computes this list and is authoritative. The triggers are:
     - *Contract-change trigger*: adding, removing or renaming a source file, a public function (a module-level name not starting with `_`) or its parameters, a CLI flag, a file format, or a data schema.
     - *Failure trigger*: a failing test, a gate script exiting non-zero, a build error, or an unhandled exception. Pass the failing output to `--involved`; any principle ID it contains is involved.
     - *Ambiguity trigger*: the request or the capsules allow two or more implementations that differ in return values, printed output, files written, exit codes, CLI flags or persisted data. If the involved sections do not settle the choice, the agent MUST ask the user (PRINCIPLE-003 R6) and MUST NOT pick one silently.
     The agent MAY read a section at any other time. The agent MUST NOT load `GUIDELINES.md` in full unless the user explicitly asks; reading every principle section one after another counts as loading it in full.
  4. **Universal vs. Domain Rule Partitioning** *[Maintainer]*:
     - *Tier 1A* is the universal principles in `GUIDELINES.md`. Their size is limited by R6: with no domain file present, every Tier 1 file MUST still fit a full Tier 1B block.
     - *Tier 1B* is the rules of the repository that holds `GUIDELINES.md` (an adopter's own rules, or in the AIKit folder rules for everything worked on from it) in `.agents/rules/domain.md`, at most 1,200 characters (300 estimated tokens), started from `.agents/rules/domain.md.template` and injected below Tier 1A in every Tier 1 file.

They never enter a Tier 1 file: `python aikit.py status <name>` and `resume <name>` print them, and the project's guidelines gate rejects a malformed rule or one worded to override a principle. They rank below Tier 1A and Tier 1B (PRINCIPLE-000 R6).
     - *Tier 2* for a project is its architecture, schemas and API specifications in `knowledge/`.
  5. **Deterministic Grep Anchor Contract** *[Agent + Maintainer]*: Every principle MUST have exactly one heading of the form `### PRINCIPLE-NNN: Title` in `GUIDELINES.md`, where NNN is three digits; `NNN` is the only placeholder used for an ID. IDs MUST NOT be renumbered or reused. To read a principle, search for the literal text `### PRINCIPLE-NNN:` with any text-search tool and read from that line up to the next line that starts with `### `, `## ` or `---`. Agents MUST NOT rely on remembered line numbers.
  6. **Strict Injected Context Budget & Automated Gate** *[Maintainer]*: Estimated tokens are the character count divided by 4, rounded down. Each Tier 1 file MUST be at most 1,600 estimated tokens including its Tier 1B block, and with no domain file present MUST still fit a 1,200-character Tier 1B block within 1,600. `python scripts/sync_principles.py` and its `--check` mode exit 1 on either breach, and the breach blocks the commit through gate (2) of PRINCIPLE-018 R3. The warning at 1,440 estimated tokens (90%) is advisory and is evaluated only after both blocking checks.
  7. **Single Source & No Decoration** *[Maintainer]*: Rule text exists only in `GUIDELINES.md`. Other files MAY cite a principle by ID and MAY summarise it in one sentence or one table row, as the `README.md` principle table does, but MUST NOT copy rule text. Generated files MUST NOT use formatting that names no mechanism (bold, emoji, repeated headings).
  8. **Terse Checklist Execution** *[Agent]*: The checklists are the *Pre-Flight Checklist* and *Post-Flight Checklist* sections of `GUIDELINES.md`; reading them is allowed under R3. On a Track C task (PRINCIPLE-002 R3) the agent MUST evaluate the Pre-Flight checklist before its first file edit of the task. On Track B and Track C tasks it MUST evaluate the Post-Flight checklist before committing. Track A tasks evaluate neither. The agent MUST NOT paste either checklist into the conversation; it reports only failed or skipped items, one line each naming the principle ID, and when nothing failed it reports `checklists passed`. An item that does not apply to the task counts as passed and is not reported; *skipped* means the item applies but was not done.
  9. **Zero Context Bloat on Expansion** *[Maintainer]*: A change that raises any Tier 1 file's estimate MUST still pass both R6 checks; when it does not, the maintainer MUST shorten existing capsules by R2's deletion test until it does. `TARGET_TOKEN_BUDGET` and `MAX_DOMAIN_CHARS` MUST NOT be raised without the user's explicit approval and a new ADR in `knowledge/decisions.md`.

def _git_start(project_root: Path) -> None:
    """
    `git init`, then commit the project's memory and instructions so a new project starts clean.
    Raises when the commit cannot be made (typically no git identity): a clean baseline is required
    for delivery and the UI guard, and AIKit never invents an author.
    """
    result = _run_git(project_root, "init", "--quiet")
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise ProjectError(
            f"`git init` failed in {project_root}: {result.stderr.strip()}",
            "every project is its own git repository, separate from AIKit's.",
            "fix the git error above, then run the command again.",
        )
    stage_items = [".gitignore", "README.md", PROJECT_MEMORY_DIRNAME]
    _run_git(project_root, "add", "--", *stage_items)
    result = _run_git(project_root, "commit", "--quiet", "-m", "chore: start project with AIKit memory")
    if result.returncode != 0:
        # git's last stderr line is the cause; the lines before it are generic advice.
        cause = (result.stderr.strip().splitlines() or ["git commit failed"])[-1]
        raise ProjectError(
            f"initial commit failed: {cause}",

            "set `git config user.name` and `git config user.email` (or repo-local equivalents), "
            "then run `aikit new` again.",
        )
    return None

content.text: <total_tokens>14965574 tokens left</total_tokens>

The other AI's work is substantively **correct and better than mine in four places** — but it shipped one real process violation, and none of the three issues you raised were addressed.

## What it did

1. **Rewrote four of my unpushed commits** (`8604ef0`, `749c1b9`, `278f3f5`, `83f462a` → `53dee30`, `342ca15`, `85e7cbb`, `83b67de`). The only change: credential-shaped test fixtures re-encoded as escape sequences — `glpat-` became `glpat\x2d`. The runtime strings are identical, so behaviour is unchanged. This is almost certainly to get past GitHub push protection, which scans every pushed commit and ignores `# aikit:allow-secret`. Rewriting was the right tool for that: a forward fix wouldn't help, because the literals would still be in earlier commits.
2. **`8216db9`** — five changes in one commit: finished my budget/pointer task, plus four fixes.
3. **`9653975`** — a one-line codebase map fix.
4. **Pushed everything.** Origin moved `b73e148` → `9653975` as a fast-forward. None of my original hashes had ever been published, so nothing shared was overwritten. I never had push authorization; whether it did is for you to say.

## Verification of each change

| Change | Verdict | How I checked |
|---|---|---|
| Budget 1600 → 1750, rule text, the 90% warning recomputed to 1,575 | ✅ Correct | Same as my staged edits; parity test and `sync --check` pass |
| Runbook pointer in all 8 targets | ✅ **Better than mine** | Uses a `RUNBOOK_PATH` constant shared with the `.claude/` mirror; margin now **548 chars** |
| `status --json --exit-code` honours `--exit-code` | ✅ **Fixes my bug** | My JSON branch ignored the flag entirely, so CI got exit 0 on a dirty tree |
| `project_is_clean` includes `ledger_error` | ✅ **Fixes my bug** | Mine printed `"clean": true` while exiting 1 |
| All delegate report paths scrubbed | ✅ **Fixes my bug** | I scrubbed only `answer_text`; `--format json` and the failure path leaked raw stdout/stderr |
| Font token checked in the declaration's value only | ✅ **Fixes my bug** | Old vs new on 6 cases: only change is `font-family: Arial; color: var(--x)`, which I passed and it flags |
| `create_project` warning channel removed | ✅ Correct | Dead since my `e6e708b` made git failures raise; all 6 call sites updated |

Every behaviour fix has a test. Tip is green: 483 tests across 7 runs, all six gates.

I'll be direct: **ADR-172 and ADR-173 overclaimed.** I wrote that the payload and exit code "cannot disagree by construction" and that the sub-agent's answer was scrubbed "unconditionally" — both were true of one path and false of another.

## What it got wrong

**Five pushed commits fail their own gate.** The rewrite changed `test_kit.py`'s bytes without regenerating the codebase map, which records that size. I checked every commit:

```
53dee30  342ca15  85e7cbb  83b67de  8216db9   → STALE map
9653975                                      → ok
```

`83b67de` exits 1 on `update_knowledge_base.py --check` in an isolated worktree, confirmed. That breaks P-018 R7 (each commit verified alone), and `9653975` patches it only at the tip. My originals each passed `verify_commit.py`. The fix would have been regenerating the map inside each rewritten commit. **Since it's published, I'd leave history alone** — the tip is correct, and repairing it would take a force-push.

The other AI touched none of them; all three are still present.

**`ui finish` message — true, and worse than described.** `finish()` returns the review-missing finding *only* when `verify()` found nothing, so "the UI change is outside its contract" (`aikit_cli.py:650`) is false in exactly the case it fires. **`validate_ledger_version` — true, but I overstated it as a defect.** The code refuses anything `!=` current, and `data_models.md` says only *newer* is refused, in two places. But `test_invalid_ledger_versions_are_refused` deliberately pins `0` and `-1` — those are invalid values, not past schemas. The hazard is real but latent: the first genuine bump makes every v1 ledger unreadable, because `migrate_ledger_schema` runs *after* validation and can never upgrade across versions. Nothing changed in the repo; the tree is clean and every sandbox I built has been removed.

## Do the worktrees matter?

**No, not functionally.** They total about 7 MB. All three are on detached HEADs, so none locks a branch. Every commit they pin is already in `main`'s history, so they keep no extra objects alive. And nothing in `scripts/`, `tests/` or CI ever lists worktrees, so they can't affect a gate.

- **`aikit_verify_2se8ob_r`** (10-21) — left by a `verify_commit.py` run that was hard-killed. Its `finally` cleanup can't run on a kill. Safe to delete.
- **`aikit_baseline_budget`** (10-21) — no AIKit code creates that name, so an agent made it by hand. Safe to delete.
- **Kilo's pool worktree** — owned and managed by Kilo. **Leave it.**

The one real observation is minor: `verify_commit.py` has no startup sweep for leftovers, so each hard kill leaves ~2.7 MB in Temp. I'd only fix that if it keeps happening.

## The three findings, reproduced

**1. `ui finish` message — confirmed end to end.** I ran a real sandbox project through the real CLI, no mocks. On one tree, `ui verify` printed `[OK] UI surface verified`; seconds later `ui finish` printed `Error: the UI change is outside its contract` and told me to "revert the listed paths" when none were listed. The JSON code `ui.review-missing` is already correct; only the human text is wrong.

Correction to my last report: following the advice to run `ui abort` reverted the valid edit and closed the task, but the work is **not destroyed**. `abort` saved the full edit as `changes.patch` in Temp, recoverable with `git apply`. The harm is real but bounded.

**2. Reachability dead code — confirmed, and my recommendation reverses.** A set can only count to 1, so the guard is always true. Two corrections:

- **Cost is negligible.** My first timing (142 ms vs 11 ms) was distorted because the parser caches syntax trees and the guarded version paid for parsing first. Measured fairly, best of five in both orders, it's **17 ms vs 10 ms**.
- **Don't fix it to match its comment.** I rebuilt the handoff bug from this session, where a dict comprehension hid the producer. The current strict shield **flags** it. A version fixed to count as the comment describes **lets it through**, because `next` appears three times as a literal. Fixing it that way would weaken a safety gate. The right fix is to delete the dead code, correct the comment, and add a test so nobody "fixes" it later.

**3. Ledger version — confirmed, and the blast radius is bigger than I said.** I simulated a v2 build against copies of real ledgers:
- Both AIKit's ledger and `tally`'s are refused on read, and `save_ledger` refuses on write.
- `migrate_ledger_schema` is called **0 times**, so the upgrade path can never run.
- There are **27 ledgers, all version 1** — ADR-174's "20 projects" undercounts.
- The refusal leaves files untouched and gives a clear message. The failure mode is every ledger command stopping until the code is fixed, not data loss.

The fix I proposed, `type(v) is not int or v < 1 or v > CURRENT` in both places, still refuses every case the existing test pins (`True`, `"2"`, `2.0`, `0`, `-1`, and newer). With `CURRENT = 1` it behaves exactly as today; it only changes what a future bump does.

**The flaky test.** There was one failure in 13 full runs, and none in the 12 since. I lost its name last time, and I've now shown worktrees can't affect tests, so my guess was wrong. **The cause is unknown.** It isn't traceable to the other AI's changes either.

## Proposed next step

1. Rewrite the `ui finish` message so it says review is the only blocker, and drop the revert/abort advice for that case.
2. Delete the reachability dead code, correct the comment, and add a regression test that a hidden producer is flagged.
3. Make the ledger version check accept valid older versions on both paths (no behaviour change today). The new ADR will record the 27-ledger correction, since ADR-174 can't be edited.

Shall I go ahead with all three?

fix(ui): [milestone 1/3] finish says review is the only blocker

`ui finish` without --reviewed printed "Error: the UI change is
outside its contract", told the user to "revert the listed paths"
(none were listed) and led with `ui abort`. But finish() reports a
missing review only after verify() found nothing, so in exactly that
case the change is inside its contract. Reproduced on a real sandbox
project: `ui verify` printed [OK] and `ui finish` on the same tree
said the opposite; following the advice to run `ui abort` reverted
the valid edit and closed the task (recoverable only from a
changes.patch left in Temp).

When every finding is ui.review-missing, finish now says the change
passed verification and that only the human review is missing, and
gives the one command that closes the task. The branch keys on the
stable finding code, not the message text, so it cannot drift from
the JSON contract. Exit code stays 1 and the JSON output is unchanged;
a real contract finding keeps the full revert/allow/abort advice.

Re-verified on the sandbox after the fix: the new message, exit 1,
then `ui finish --reviewed` closes the task with the edit intact.

Phase 4 on this tree: 485 tests, rule sync, AST map, reachability,
secrets, dogfood. check_test_budgets.py failed once and passed on an
immediate re-run of the unchanged tree; it runs both tiers, which
include dogfood's --help timing track, a pre-existing flake measured
in this session (aikit.py --help has a ~160ms floor under a 200ms
single-sample budget at every revision back to 10-22).

def ledger_version_supported(version: Any) -> bool:
    """
    Whether this build can read a ledger declaring `version`: an int from 1 to the current schema.

    An older valid version is supported because `migrate_ledger_schema` upgrades it; only a newer
    one, or a value that is not a real version (`0`, `-1`, `True`, `"1"`, `1.0`), is refused.
    Both the read and the write path ask this one question: the check used to be `!=` in each,
    so the first schema bump would have refused every existing ledger (ADR-178).
    """
    return type(version) is int and 1 <= version <= LEDGER_SCHEMA_VERSION


def validate_ledger_version(data: Any, path: Path) -> None:
    """Refuse a ledger whose declared schema this build does not read (PRINCIPLE-013 R4)."""
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or "version" not in data:
        return
    version = data.get("version")
    if not ledger_version_supported(version):
        raise UnsupportedLedgerVersion(path, version, LEDGER_SCHEMA_VERSION)
